headline: On last trading day, Sensex and Nifty snapped 2-week gains as surging oil prices dragged markets down

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 26 October.

why: Surging international oil prices dragged Indian equities to weekly losses.
Persistent selling pressure led the markets to snap a two-week winning streak.
Selling pressure in earlier sessions triggered a broader market pullback.
Regulatory developments, including proposed SEBI rules on broker terminal misuse, remain in focus.
whatHappening: In the last session on October 23, Sensex closed down 125 points while Nifty settled at 22,600.
Markets saw a selective rebound driven by buying in IT stocks after a three-day losing streak.
Indian shares posted weekly losses amid geopolitical and crude oil price volatility.
Fifteen companies including Chennai Petroleum, L&T Tech, Cyient, and Nippon Life AMC are in focus for dividends.
summary: On the last trading day, Indian stock markets snapped two weeks of gains with the Sensex falling 125 points and Nifty closing at 22,600. Higher crude oil prices weighed on broader market sentiment, though buying in IT stocks offered mild support. The stock market is closed today for the weekend and will reopen on Monday, October 26.
